title: BERLIN/CLOCK as substitution + columnar role pair
hypothesis_summary: The BERLIN crib at 64-69 and the CLOCK crib at 70-74 are the two strongest plaintext anchors in real K4. A natural hand-cipher composition would place one as a substitution keyword and the other as a columnar transposition key. This pack enumerates that pairing in two-layer Vig/Beau/VarBeau columnar combinations.

provenance_items.quote_or_summary: Disclosed plaintext span BERLIN at indices 64-69 (Sanborn confirmation 2010).
Disclosed plaintext span CLOCK at indices 70-74 (Sanborn confirmation 2014).

composition_templates.rationale: Two-layer keyword sub + keyed columnar — the simplest hand cipher compatible with two named clue keywords.

constraints: Both keywords must be tried in both substitution and columnar roles (LESSON-010 i3 generator handles this).
caveats: BERLIN/CLOCK are KNOWN plaintext spans, not necessarily keys. The pack is testing whether they could ALSO function as keys — a structurally independent question.
Tier-1 evidence on the spans does NOT translate to tier-1 evidence on a key role.
